record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.context_brief: Characteristic factors for commuting polynomial averages
record.original_question: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are pairwise independent integer polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. Does there exist d such that the Host-Kra factors Z_{d,T1}, ..., Z_{d,Tℓ} are characteristic for the polynomial averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Suppose that the polynomials p1, . . . , p` ∈ Z[t] are pairwise independent. Show that there exists d ∈ N such that the factors Zd,T1, . . . , Zd,T` are characteristic factors for the averages (17).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$. For a single measure-preserving transformation $T$ and an integer $d\ge 0$, let $Z_{d,T}$ denote the $d$-th Host–Kra factor of the system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ (the factor characterized by the property that a bounded function $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}(f\mid Z_{d,T})=0$ if and only if its $(d+1)$-th Host–Kra–Gowers seminorm $\|f\|_{U^{d+1}(T)}$ vanishes).

Call integer polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ pairwise independent if for every $i\neq j$ the polynomials $p_i,p_j$ and the constant polynomial $1$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, $p_i$, $p_j$, $p_i-p_j$ are all non-constant).

A family of factors $(Y_1,\dots,Y_\ell)$ (with $Y_i$ a $T_i$-invariant sub-$\sigma$-algebra) is called characteristic for the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)\;=\;\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \big(T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1\big)\cdots\big(T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell\big)$$
if, for all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\Big\|A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)-A_N\big(\mathbb{E}(f_1\mid Y_1),\dots,\mathbb{E}(f_\ell\mid Y_\ell)\big)\Big\|_{L^2(\mu)}=0.$$

Problem. Show that there exists $d\in\mathbb{N}$ (depending only on $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ and $\ell$) such that for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ as above, the factors $Z_{d,T_1},\dots,Z_{d,T_\ell}$ are characteristic for the averages $A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Frantzikinakis and Kuca (arXiv:2207.12288, "Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences", 2022) proves that the Host–Kra factor is characteristic for multiple ergodic averages of commuting transformations along pairwise independent integer polynomials, without extra assumptions on the system. This appears to resolve the problem affirmatively. Related follow-up work (e.g., arXiv:2209.11033, arXiv:2410.15130) treats the pairwise dependent case.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the Host-Kra factor is characteristic for pairwise independent polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that Host–Kra factors are characteristic for commuting transformations along pairwise independent integer polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Seminorm control for ergodic averages with commuting transformations along pairwise dependent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple ergodic averages of commuting transformations with polynomial iterates ... are controlled by the Gowers-Host-Kra seminorms.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work extends Host–Kra seminorm control to pairwise dependent polynomials, building on the pairwise independent case.
